I paid for a yearly subscription to Cal AI and genuinely regret it. The entire point of using a nutrition-tracking app is to make tracking easier and more accurate, but I constantly have to double-check and correct this app.  Even when I scan the actual nutrition label, it frequently enters values that do not match the label right in front of me. I would estimate that 9 out of 10 products I scan require some kind of manual correction. At that point, what exactly is the AI saving me?  The Food Score is even more frustrating. The app repeatedly tells me that I am low on protein when my logged numbers clearly show that I have met or even exceeded the protein goal already set in the app. Foods can also receive poor scores because Cal AI fails to properly calculate things like fiber, sugar, and sodium. Worse, when I manually correct inaccurate nutrition information, the scoring system still does not seem to properly account for those corrections.  That makes the score feel arbitrary rather than useful. A nutrition app should not penalize a food because the app itself failed to capture its nutritional information correctly.  For a paid product—especially an annual subscription—basic nutrition-label scanning and macro calculations should be reliable. I should not have to audit nearly every entry against the package.  At this point, the only reason I continue using Cal AI is to maintain a rough idea of how many calories I am eating. I do not trust it enough for accurate macro or micronutrient tracking, and I definitely do not trust its Food Score.  I wish I had not purchased the yearly subscription. The concept is great, but the execution has been extremely disappointing.

I've been using this app for over 6 months  now.   It's got some neat features, but a few problems.  In addition to the messed up work flow issues I detailed below, one of the built-in features just doesn’t work.  I cannot export my data.    I have put in a ticket at least three times now.  Each time, I send them a screenshot and info on my device type/sw.   Then crickets.  I can live with all of the other issues, but being ignored by tech support is what’s causing me to downgrade this rating.    This app recently sold for a *lot* of money.  You’d think with that kind of investment, they could put a few dollars into development.    Here’s my comments from the 4 week mark:  The work flow is really poor.  For example, if you want to enter a recipe, you have to go to "Saved Foods" and then "My Meals".  This was not obvious the first time I tried it (nor does it not make sense.)  Then, if I want to create a recipe (or, "meal" as they call it) I can add something from "Saved Foods" or "My Foods".  It is not intuitively obvious what "My Foods" is for or how it differs from "Saved Foods."  If I want to add an item to a recipe that I physically have in front of me, I have to add it to "Saved Meals" first.  To add something to "Saved Meals", you apparently have to add it to your current meal, save it, then delete it.  Maybe there's another way,but again, not intuitively obvious.    Another issue is serving size.  If I add an item to "Saved Foods", it doesn't put anywhere in the description or data what that serving size was.  So if I eat it at a later time, when I pull it up, I don't know what they considered as a serving size.  Yes, sometimes it lets me go in and put in a specific measure (oz, cups, etc.), but if say, the serving size was based on a number of pieces (let's say 6 for an example), then I add it to my day's intake but only ate say 3 pieces, there's no way to know that the nutrition was based on 6 pieces.  I work around this by editing the item name and putting the serving size in the description.  I shouldn't have to do this.  The information is obviously there.  Let us use it.  Finally, the "Saved Foods" list just grows and grows.  Yes, there is a search function, but you don't always hit the search term correctly, so you either have to try multiple times, or scroll through an ever growing long list.  It would be nice to be able to organize and sort this list so I can access it easily.  I'm sure there's things I haven't figured out yet, but it shouldn't be that way.  If something isn't intuitive, there needs to be instructions.  Just because the developers think their app works fine doesn't mean it does if you weren't in on developing it.  It's like this app never went through a real beta test, or else the developers don't really use it themselves.  This could be a good app, but like I said - work flow. It's not right,

I appreciate that this app is streamlined, and easy to use. It would be great if it tracked fat as a macro.  One thing to watch out for is the  “Recent Meals” feature on food tracking. Understand that it is not just a list of foods in standard serving sizes, but macros for the food in the quantity you last recorded.   For example, you search the database and find the information for one cup of whole milk. But you drink a half a cup of milk and so record .5 servings. Now the .5 servings is the nutritional information stored in “Recent Meals.”   The next time you pull whole milk off “Recent Meals” for a new diary entry it will pull that half cup “meal” up and show it as one serving. If you assume, as I did, that was indicating the standard serving from the nutritional database (1 cup) you will be off by 50%.  What would be more useful, in my opinion, is Quick access to “Recent FOODS,” with the macros corresponding to a standard serving size that is easy to see: “Whole Milk, 1c.”   The way it is now you have to look up everything every time, which is a drag.
